open_obligations: Check that Kenton et al.'s judges were indeed used without persona or belief conditioning
Confirm that the 'default LM judges' compared here are run by the authors on their own COVID-19 claims, not taken from Kenton et al.
Note that in some of Rahman et al.'s conditions the debaters are aware of the judge personas, a change beyond conditioning the judge
Check whether Rahman et al.'s GPT-4o and Qwen-2.5-7B judges are less capable than their debaters, as the judge in Kenton et al.'s comparison is ('a less capable judge')
out.other_title: Assigned-role consultancy and debate with an LLM judge, compared with direct QA baselines
out.rationale: The authors build on the LLM-judge setup of the cited oversight studies and name the change (persona conditioning), comparing against the conventional version in their own experiments. That is EXTENDS; it does not dispute Kenton et al.'s results, which come from different tasks.
out.scope: proposed EXTENDS: How LLM judges are configured in debate and consultancy experiments; the change is conditioning the judge on a persona with prior beliefs

text: The authors describe standard LLM judges without persona conditioning as the conventional approach used in previous oversight studies [30, 31], and run them as an alternative evaluation. They report that persona-based LLM judges outperform both human judges and these default LLM judges in supervising unreliable experts.
title: Persona conditioning added to the plain LLM judges of previous oversight studies [30, 31]
